faq.answer_text: The certification exam covers a total of four distinct domains, which include the SAP Enterprise Architecture Framework and Toolset, Architecture Vision and Roadmap, Business Architecture, and Data, Application, and Technology Architecture.
faq.question_title: How many domains are covered on the exam?

faq.answer_text: The passing score for the SAP Certified Professional - SAP Enterprise Architect assessment is set at precisely 60 percent to successfully demonstrate professional competency and architectural knowledge.
The exam has a total duration of 120 minutes, giving all candidates sufficient time to complete every professional-level scenario question presented during the evaluation process successfully.

Yes, this exam is current and active for professionals seeking certification. If you need any further information regarding long-term certification pathways and official updates, check with SAP directly.

editorial.overview: The SAP Certified Professional - SAP Enterprise Architect certification validates your professional-level expertise in enterprise architecture frameworks, business architecture, roadmap development, and technical solutions. Certified by SAP, this scenario-based assessment evaluates your ability to correctly interpret complex IT requirements and apply reference architectures effectively across modern enterprise systems during the 120-minute assessment.
editorial.preparation_strategy: To adequately prepare for this professional-level assessment, review the official exam guide and study all related architecture framework documentation. Focus specifically on understanding how to map business capabilities, interpret IT requirements, and structure enterprise architecture models using the available reference content and frameworks provided by SAP.
editorial.who_should_take: Enterprise architects, solution architects, and senior consultants with experience in SAP technologies should take this 120-minute professional-level assessment to demonstrate expertise in designing architectures and roadmaps.
